name: Neil Movva
milestone_by_age_26: At 28, co-founded and led Sail Research when it disclosed $80 million in seed and Series A funding at a reported $450 million valuation.
early_history_summary: Studied electrical engineering at Stanford, completed BS and MS degrees in 2019, and worked on deep-learning performance at NVIDIA before joining Apple. His documented work moved across GPU kernels, accelerated visual computing, robotics, privacy-preserving systems, and AI inference infrastructure.
family_context_summary: Family financial position and inherited business networks were not documented in the reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parental or close-family domain advantage was not documented in the reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford engineering, NVIDIA and Apple systems work, long-term cofounder
evidence_summary: Movva's path combines selective technical institutions, repeated work close to AI hardware and inference, and a long-running collaboration with Samir Menon. NVIDIA and Apple supplied unusually direct contact with accelerated computing; Stanford supplied research infrastructure and the peer relationship that later became a founding team. Sail's funding is treated as a documented company outcome and discovery signal, not proof that capital raised measures personal merit or future success.
starting_point: Family origin was not documented in reviewed sources; attended the Harker School before Stanford.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Sail Research, an AI-infrastructure company that disclosed $80 million in funding in 2026.
